newsitem.title: USA: Pepsi to sell PFS unit to AmeriServe.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi to sell PFS unit to AmeriServe.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc said it reached a definitive agreement to sell its PFS restaurant supply distribution unit to AmeriServe Food Distribution Inc, a subsidiary of Holberg Industries Inc, for undisclosed terms.

The combination of AmeriServe and PFS would create the largest foodservice systems distributor in the United States, with more than 5,000 employees and expected 1997 sales in excess of $5.4 billion, the companies said in a statement.
It would serve over 28,000 restaurants, they said.
PFS, based in Dallas, distributes about $3.4 billion worth of food, equipment and other supplies to around 18,000 restaurants in the United States and Canada, Pepsi said.
It mostly served PepsiCo's restaurant chains -- Pizza Hut, KFC and Taco Bell, it said.
Brookfield, Wisconsin-based AmeriServe, with expected 1997 sales of $2.0 billion, is one of the largest foodservice systems distributors in the United States, the company said.
It said it served over 10,000 restaurants, including Wendy's, Grand Metropolitan Plc's Burger King, Arby's, Dairy Queen, Applebee's, Godfather's Pizza and nearly 800 KFC restaurants.

The sale was part of a major strategic effort announced in January under which PepsiCo has focused on its Frito-Lay snack and Pepsi-Cola beverage businesses by spinning-off its three large restaurant chains to shareholders and selling its smaller restaurant chains and PFS.
The sale was expected to close in the next several weeks, the companies said.
